chunks: Ali (peace be upon him) from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Aban al-Ahmar, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:

"Whoever is granted freedom (or inherits) on an estate before the estate is divided, it is for him; and whoever is granted freedom (or inherits) after the estate is divided, he has no share in the estate. And whoever is manumitted on an estate before the estate is divided, he is free; and whoever is manumitted after the estate is divided, he has no share in the estate."
And he said regarding the woman: 'If she is granted freedom before the estate is divided, she has the estate.'

key_terms.أَسْلَمَ: He became Muslim (or was granted freedom in context)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on inheritance if a heir converts to Islam or is manumitted after the estate has already been divided?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the temporal condition for inheriting from a mixed-faith estate, establishing that conversion to Islam or manumission must occur prior to the physical division of the estate to be valid. It specifically extends this ruling to women, ensuring their inheritance rights are preserved under the same pre-division condition, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that the status of the heir is fixed at the time of the estate's distribution.
